findings.claim_broken: Stale against D2 head. Since 1a95bd1 (OB-1) `OutboxRelay.rebuild()` is since=db_now → snapshot → index.rebuild → reopen_dispatch(since) → pump: rows acknowledged/claimed at/after `since` whose job still wants dispatch (no live lease of either kind) become pending again and the pump re-enqueues them. That closes the same "delivered behind a stale snapshot, then wiped" hole by a different mechanism. Comparison: Q3's second snapshot is state-based (every job wanted after the rebuild, regardless of when its row was acked), so it also covers an ack whose transaction began before `since` and committed after the snapshot (D2's `>= since` bound assumes acks start after the snapshot statement, which a single-statement ack makes practically but not strictly true); D2's reopen leaves an outbox audit trail and re-sends only what it changed. Neither covers the acked-then-rebuilt case (worker acks in the index after the rebuild) — only Q3's next reconcile pass (blocked → rebuild) does, so the request to make OutboxRelay delegate to Reconciler still stands, but not for the reason given. Signatures: at both 8728aec and ebb3c86, PgJobStore exposes exactly dispatch_pending(*, limit: int = 100, worker_id: str = "relay", redelivery_s: float = 30.0) -> tuple[IndexEvent, ...], acknowledge_dispatch(event_ids) -> int, dispatch_snapshot() -> tuple[IndexEvent, ...] — request 1's claim holds.
findings.evidence: codex-d2 outbox.py lines 69-74; 0012 lines 352-376; git log -S reopen_dispatch → 1a95bd1; tests/d/test_adapter_units.py:257 asserts order [since, snapshot, rebuild, reopen:t0, pump]; jobstore.py lines 235-268 at HEAD and `git show 8728aec:…jobstore.py` lines 235-248.
findings.minimal_fix: Amend request 1: "D2's rebuild fences with reopen_dispatch(since) (OB-1); Q3's second-snapshot top-up is equivalent for that hole and additionally state-based; the acked-then-rebuilt case needs the reconciler pass either way. Integration: run one relay (Reconciler), or have OutboxRelay.rebuild call Reconciler.rebuild." Also note that Q3's drain never calls release_dispatch (a deferred row waits a full redelivery_s, 30 s, even when a slot frees earlier — OB-4's latency point) nor fail_dispatch.

findings.claim_broken: The fake reaper (`recover()`) emits a NEW event id on every requeue (prepare_dispatch at 1002, inference_dispatch at 1039); at D2 head no SQL writes any dispatch row outside admit (0011:350) and prepare (0012:233) — there is no SQL reaper (D3). So test_q3_reconcile__a_job_redispatched_during_the_pass_keeps_its_new_candidate and the differential's `recover` op run on a requeue semantics PostgreSQL does not have yet; on the real store a preparing job whose lease expired keeps only its ORIGINAL event id, the W2 loop has acked it in the index (memory.py:168 / Q2 ACKED set refuses a replay), and every reconcile pass until it is re-prepared reports it `blocked` and rebuilds (fairness reset). Q3's request that D3's reaper write a new event id therefore does follow from Q2's acked-set semantics and is load-bearing, not optional.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "'prepare_dispatch'" codex-d2 migrations | insert → only 0011:350; no create function infrx.recover/reap; memory.py line 168 `if event.event_id in self._entries or event.event_id in self.acknowledged: return False`; Q2 evidence r2 limits: "The ACKED set grows until the next rebuild".
findings.minimal_fix: Record in Q3's evidence that the fake's `recover()` new-id behaviour is a D3 requirement the SQL does not yet meet, and that until D3 lands each lost preparation worker costs one rebuild per job (bounded by the number of lost leases, never a lost job).

findings.claim_broken: Error mapping: the fake's lost-ack fault is `OutboxLost(ConnectionError)`; PgJobStore._call maps only P0001/23514/55000/P0002/22023 and returns any other psycopg error raw (jobstore.py:69-91), so a real lost connection is `psycopg.OperationalError` — neither ConnectionError nor OSError — and `dispatch_snapshot` goes through `_query`, which applies no mapping at all. findings.claim_broken: run(): "A failure of either - Valkey restarting, PostgreSQL unreachable - is logged, counted and retried at the next tick (a failed pass stays due): the relay has to outlive the outages it exists to repair." A persistently failing reconcile() (unbounded dispatch_snapshot timing out under a backlog - the lane's own Limit 4 - or one poison snapshot row that enqueue rejects) silently disables drain(): both calls sit in one try, reconcile runs first, and because the failed pass "stays due" every subsequent tick retries reconcile and never reaches drain. No new dispatch is delivered while the condition lasts; every queued job then ends queue_wait_expired. No test exercises a reconcile-only persistent failure (the run() case uses a one-shot outage).
findings.evidence: Reviewer probe tests/q/review_starve.py (memory adapter, store whose dispatch_snapshot always raises ConnectionError, run(stop, drain_every_s=0.001, reconcile_every_s=0.01) for 0.5 s, 3 jobs admitted): `errors 278 members 0 unacked 3`. Same probe after the minimal fix below: `errors 333 members 3 unacked 0` - the drain delivered everything despite every pass failing.
findings.minimal_fix: Two try blocks in run(): wrap `await self.reconcile(); due = ...` in its own try/except (count + log) and `await self.drain()` in a second one, so a failing pass never skips the drain. Add a case: Interleave whose action always raises on dispatch_snapshot, run() for a few ticks, assert members == the admitted jobs and unacknowledged() == []; add the matching mutant (fold the two try blocks back into one) to reconcile_mutants.py.

findings.claim_broken: switch(): "topped up from a snapshot read AFTER the swap" (docstring and evidence item 3). Only the presence of the top-up is pinned; its order relative to `self.index = index` is not. Reviewer mutant R10 (top-up snapshot read BEFORE the swap) survived the lane's suite; a drain delivering between that snapshot and the swap lands in the old index and reaches the new one only at the next reconcile pass (one reconcile_every_s of delay, not a loss). The lane's Interleave at n=2 cannot see it; at n=3 it can.
findings.evidence: runB1b on 55751: `[survived] R10_the_switch_tops_up_from_a_snapshot_read_before_the_swap: 2 passed`; the same edit against the reviewer's n=3 case: `[killed] R10b_...__reviewer_case: 2 failed`. The added case passes on the unmutated code (`2 passed` on both adapters).
findings.minimal_fix: Add the n=3 interleave case (test_review_switch__a_delivery_between_the_post_swap_snapshot_and_the_swap, body in this report's mutant table) to tests/q/test_reconcile.py and the ordering mutant to reconcile_mutants.py.

findings.claim_broken: Metric honesty: `outbox_lag_s` is "the age of the oldest dispatch row the drain found waiting"; it is only written when a read returns rows, so after the backlog clears the gauge keeps reporting the last non-zero lag indefinitely.
findings.evidence: Probe: after a drain that found a 9 s row `outbox_lag_s == 9.0`; after the next, empty, drain still `9.0`.
findings.minimal_fix: Set `self.metrics["outbox_lag_s"] = 0.0` at the top of drain() (or when `events` is empty); extend test_q3_metrics__the_outbox_lag_is_the_oldest_waiting_dispatch with one empty drain and assert 0.0.

findings.claim_broken: rebuild() discards the `blocked` count of its own top-up. A worker acknowledging a candidate between the rebuild (acked set cleared, candidate re-indexed) and the top-up's enqueue leaves the job unindexed until the next reconcile pass, which then rebuilds again (documented as 'the other half of the hole'; self-healing, bounded by reconcile_every_s).
findings.evidence: Reviewer race2 on real Valkey: `rebuild returned 1; members after rebuild {}` then `next pass {'missing': 1, 'rebuilt': 1}; members {…: job}`.
findings.minimal_fix: Have rebuild() re-run the top-up once when `report["blocked"]` is non-zero (or return it so reconcile() rebuilds in the same pass); assert in the drill case that members holds the job immediately after rebuild().

findings.claim_broken: "D2's OutboxRelay ... its rebuild lacks the post-rebuild top-up, which leaves Q2's hole open." D2's rebuild closes the same hole by a different fence: db_now() BEFORE the snapshot, rebuild, then reopen_dispatch(since) so every row acked/claimed since is pending again and the next pump re-sends it (index acked set cleared by the rebuild). The two designs are alternatives, not a defect in D2; the integration request should say which one the merged relay keeps (Q3's needs no SQL; D2's also covers a second relay process).
findings.evidence: codex-d2 infrx/state/outbox.py:69-72 (`since = await self.store.db_now()`, `rebuild(dispatch_snapshot())`, `reopen_dispatch(since)`), 0012_dispatch_outbox.sql reopen_dispatch comment (review OB-1).
findings.minimal_fix: Reword handback 1: replace or delegate, but not on the grounds that D2 leaves the hole open; note that Reconciler.rebuild also does not call reopen_dispatch, so with two relay processes only one of the two fences is in force.

findings.claim_broken: Drain retry latency: rows the index refused (capacity_exhausted) or that an outage cut off stay claimed for the full redelivery_s (30 s) because the drain never calls D2's release_dispatch (review OB-4) and never records the refusal with fail_dispatch (OB-7). Not a loss - the redelivery test proves the retry - but a 30 s stall per refused row while the store offers an immediate hand-back.
findings.evidence: reconcile.py drain() uses only dispatch_pending/acknowledge_dispatch; 0012 defines release_dispatch/fail_dispatch; FakeDispatchOutbox implements neither, so nothing in tests/q could exercise them.
findings.minimal_fix: On CapacityExhausted (and in the outage `finally`) call `store.release_dispatch(deferred_ids)` when the store has it; add both functions to outboxfake.py row for row.

A persistently failing reconcile() (unbounded dispatch_snapshot timing out under a backlog - the lane's own Limit 4 - or one poison snapshot row that enqueue rejects) silently disables drain(): both calls sit in one try, reconcile runs first, and because the failed pass "stays due" every subsequent tick retries reconcile and never reaches drain. votes.reason: Confirmed at 152de7e by code reading and by reproducing the probe in a scratch archive. `Reconciler.run()` (apps/infrx-api/infrx/scheduling/reconcile.py lines 72-80) puts `reconcile()` and `drain()` in one try block with reconcile first and `due` only advanced after reconcile returns. If `reconcile()` raises, `due` is never advanced, so every subsequent tick re-enters reconcile, raises again, and `drain()` is never reached. Probe (memory adapter, store whose `dispatch_snapshot` always raises ConnectionError, 3 jobs admitted, `run(stop, drain_every_s=0.001, reconcile_every_s=0.01)` for 0.5 s): at 152de7e `errors 372 members 0 unacked 3` - no dispatch delivered. With the reviewer's minimal fix (two try blocks) applied in scratch: `errors 371 members 3 unacked 0` - drain delivered everything despite every reconcile failing. This breaks the docstring's own claim that a failed pass is "retried at the next tick" and the relay "outlives the outages it exists to repair": a persistently failing reconcile (e.g. the unbounded `dispatch_snapshot()` timing out under backlog while `dispatch_pending(limit=100)` would succeed, or a snapshot event whose `enqueue` raises anything other than CapacityExhausted in `_top_up`) silently disables all new dispatch until the process restarts. The only existing run() test (`test_q3_run__the_relay_reconciles_first_and_retries_a_failed_pass`) uses a one-shot `Interleave(..., 1, outage)`, so the starvation path has no killable test; the reconcile_mutants list has no mutant for it either. Not a box-safety hazard, but a real durability defect on the invariant the module exists to hold, with no test that would catch it. Scratch removed.

Confirmed at 152de7e. apps/infrx-api/infrx/scheduling/reconcile.py lines 72-80: `reconcile()` and `drain()` share one try; when reconcile raises, `due` is never advanced, so every tick re-enters `if loop.time() >= due`, calls reconcile first, raises again, and `drain()` is never reached for as long as the reconcile failure persists. This directly contradicts the run() docstring ("a failure of either ... is retried at the next tick") - drain is not retried at all. Reproduced with the reviewer's probe shape in a scratch archive of 152de7e (memory adapter, store whose dispatch_snapshot always raises ConnectionError, 3 jobs admitted, run(stop, drain_every_s=0.001, reconcile_every_s=0.01) for 0.5 s): `errors 321 members 0 unacked 3` - nothing delivered. With the reviewer's minimal fix (separate try blocks for reconcile and drain): `errors 429 members 3 unacked 0` - all delivered despite every reconcile failing. The failure mode is realistic and distinct from a full PostgreSQL outage: dispatch_snapshot is an unbounded query (the lane's own Limit 4) while dispatch_pending is limited, so a snapshot timeout under backlog stalls all dispatch while the limited drain would still work; an index.members() failure or a poison row rejected by enqueue in _top_up does the same. Existing test test_q3_run__the_relay_reconciles_first_and_retries_a_failed_pass only uses a one-shot outage (Interleave(..., 1, outage)), so no test kills this. Blocking: real liveness defect (queued jobs sit until queue_wait_expired) violating a stated invariant, with no killable test.
